$comment: WORKED EXAMPLE for WP-V0.0 — see README.md. Every clip below has placeholder:true because no audio is attached. This file shows the manifest schema (manifest.schema.json) populated with realistic reference text, so a human curating the real corpus has a template for tone/length/tagging, not a blank form. DO NOT run the bench harness against this file expecting real numbers — fixtures/voice/wer.ts skips placeholder rows and will report an empty result set if every clip is a placeholder.
notes: Replace this file's role once real clips exist: keep the schema, delete the $comment, set placeholder:false per clip as audio is recorded and human-verified.

clips.reference_text: Can you ping Siobhan about the Kubernetes rollout before Thursday's standup
clips.notes: 'Siobhan' is the canonical hard case for phonetic mismatch — /ʃɪˈvɔːn/ has no orthographic relationship to its sound. This is exactly the bias-term-mismatch scenario SPEC 3.3 calls out.

clips.reference_text: Set the env var DATABASE_URL to postgres colon slash slash localhost five four three two slash myapp underscore dev
clips.notes: Deliberately dictated as spoken punctuation ('colon slash slash') rather than natural reading — tests literal bias-layer-2 substitution rules (SPEC 3.3 layer 2: 'cursor dot ai' -> 'cursor.ai').

clips.reference_text: The bug is in useEffect inside handleSubmit, we're calling setState after unmount
clips.notes: camelCase identifiers spoken as natural words ('use effect', 'handle submit') — tests whether bias correction recovers the coding-convention casing, an AppKind::Code scenario.

clips.reference_text: I think we should schedule the review for next Tuesday afternoon if that works for everyone
clips.notes: No bias terms on purpose — isolates raw acoustic-model accent robustness from the bias pipeline's effect. Pair with accented-en-02 (same speaker, WITH bias terms) to separate the two variables.

clips.reference_text: Please loop in Nguyen and Xiaoyu before we merge the pull request into main
clips.notes: Same speaker/accent as accented-en-01, but stacks a second hard slice (proper-noun) — this intersection is where SPEC §7 expects local ASR to hurt most.

clips.reference_text: Don't wake the baby, tell them the meeting moved to four thirty
clips.notes: Whispered speech lacks fundamental frequency (F0) entirely, not just low volume — a naive gain-normalization test fixture would not exercise the same failure mode. Real recording must be an actual whisper, not a quiet normal-voice take.

clips.reference_text: The password is on the sticky note under the Anthropic mug
clips.notes: Whispered + proper-noun stack. Also a good secure-context adjacent example for the commands-side fixtures (dictation content near a password mention, not a command — kept here purely as an ASR hard case).

clips.reference_text: Thanks for sending that over, I'll take a look this afternoon and get back to you tomorrow
clips.notes: Plain casual-prose control clip — no hard-slice tags, no bias terms. Belongs in the corpus so the run matrix has a general-traffic WER number alongside the hard-slice numbers (SPEC §7: 'general-traffic WER will look fine and hide this').
